newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria OMV to expand E&P in N.Africa, Albania.
newsitem.headline: Austria OMV to expand E&P in N.Africa, Albania.

text.p: Austrian oil group OMV AG is hoping to start an onshore drill in Albania early this year and is eyeing Algeria and Egypt as possible sites for future bores, chief executive Richard Schenz said on Wednesday.

Some 4.5 billion schillings in investments over the next three years should help to expand OMV's exploration and production beyond its main existing fields in Austria, Libya and the North Sea, he continued.

The firm has set itself a target of adding 20,000 barrels per day (bpd) to its crude oil ouput by the end of 1998, taking total production to 80,000 bpd. Eventually it aims to pump around 100,000 bpd.

"We are in negotiations (with the Albanian government) on production sharing and we are hoping to strike a deal at the end of March so that we can start drilling," chief executive Richard Schenz told the club of economic journalists.
OMV has a 50 percent stake in the onshore block. Britain's Enterprise Oil Plc is represented with 30 percent, Clyde Petroleum Plc with 15 percent and Hungary's MOL with five percent.
Test drills off the Albanian coast last year were unsuccessful.

Schenz said OMV was considering extending its north African exploration and production activities into Egypt and Algeria. The firm is already developing Libya's Murzuk field with France's Total and Spain's Repsol.
"We are looking at (Egypt and Algeria)," Schenz said, without giving further details.
OMV would press on with last year's successful drilling programme in Austria and planned up to seven bores, he continued.
The firm had enjoyed less success with test drills in Vietnam and would probably pull out in the near future.
